prize_parts.citation: for discoveries establishing GLP-1 as an incretin hormone and defining its active form and physiological actions, which opened the way to incretin-based treatment of diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: a single-part prize on B012 naming Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. The round-1 exchange tested the weaknesses and did not overturn the merit case. The chain from proglucagon processing, through the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide and the human incretin physiology, to the demonstration that the hormone's actions can be exploited pharmacologically is complete, independently confirmed, and now supported by large randomized outcome trials in diabetes, obesity, and cardiovascular and renal disease. Nobody questioned maturity. A single part is also the only honest configuration under the three-person ceiling. Pairing B012 with B024 would mean five names, and trimming B012 to make room would break the credit chain I consider its strongest feature. I would not trade scientific coherence for a balanced-looking pair.
statement.case_against: The attribution problems are real and remain open. Mojsov's priority for the active peptide is contested relative to Habener and colleagues, who are not on the supplied credit list, and nothing in the files lets me settle it. Knudsen is excluded, although protraction chemistry that turned a peptide with a half-life of minutes into a once-weekly medicine is more than routine translation, as Linnarsson and Svenningsson argued. If the committee decides the prize should reward the therapeutic achievement, my trio is the wrong one and Knudsen would have to replace a name. Finally, a single-part prize leaves the unfolded protein response, which I regard as the strongest purely mechanistic case, unrewarded this year. I accept that cost as a consequence of the name limit, not as a judgment on B024's merit.

responses.point: Sten argued that protraction chemistry is more than routine translation and that a physiology-based citation is defensible only if it openly says it does not capture the drug-engineering step. He would not accept Knudsen at the expense of the basic names.
responses.response: I agree with both halves and have changed the citation in response. It now says the discoveries established GLP-1 as an incretin hormone and defined its active form and actions, and that this opened the way to therapy. It claims no credit for making the therapy. I do not think the citation text can carry an explicit disclaimer about Knudsen, since Nobel citations are short, but the claim it makes is deliberately limited to discovery. I also take your point that B024 would sit better beside a clinical part than alone. That is a reason to keep it as my first alternative, but it does not solve the five-name problem.

responses.point: Thomas would reopen Knudsen's place if Mojsov's priority proves weaker than the record suggests, would not widen the prize to four, and sees B024 as the cleaner basic-science second part if one is wanted.
responses.response: We agree that a fourth name is off the table and that Mojsov's standing is the hinge. The round-1 files give the committee no new evidence on it, so the question stays open. My position is that a defensible Mojsov credit rests on the synthesis and identification of the active 7-36 peptide as a separate contribution, and I would keep her unless the priority evidence became clearly adverse. If it did, I would substitute Knudsen for her and not widen the list. On B024 as a second part, I think your point is right on attribution but the three-person ceiling makes it unworkable beside B012, and I do not think a clean credit list justifies cutting the GLP-1 chain.

responses.point: Marie said the absence of translation is not neutral for B024, since its disease payoff is largely prospective, and that she weighs it against candidates whose mechanism has already changed treatment. She also moved toward the two-name June and Sadelain version of B009.
responses.response: I accept that the argument for B024 is weaker than I put it in round 1 if the prize is meant to reflect demonstrated benefit. Translation is early, and I now describe B024 as a strong alternative, not a co-equal part. I still think a basic mechanism need not wait for a drug, and that clean attribution is the reason to keep it available. On B009, your move to two names is sensible, but it leaves Eshhar unresolved, as you say, and I regard that as disqualifying for a second part this year unless the committee can resolve it. I place B009 as my second alternative, behind B024.

responses.point: Per's round-2 questions ask whether the committee can settle Mojsov versus Habener, and whether a second part is warranted, given that Eshhar, Rosenberg and the PERK arm are all contested.
responses.response: On Mojsov versus Habener, I cannot settle it from the files and will not pretend to. The defensible position is that GLP-1 credit is not a single-name priority question. Holst's physiology and Drucker's biology stand without Mojsov, which limits the damage if her priority is disputed. On a second part, I do not see one that is clean enough. B024 has the best attribution but the Ron and PERK omission limits it, B009 has the Eshhar and Rosenberg problems, and B016 and B046 give the drug-versus-discovery tension in a sharper form than B012. A single strong part is better than a pair with a visible weakness. I also agree with you that B016 is mature, but my reservation about credit for the oncogene discovery stands.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's identification of the active GLP-1 peptide is independent and substantial enough relative to Habener and colleagues, who are not on the credited list. I cannot verify this from the files.

Whether the committee wants to honour physiology and peptide biology or the drug-development step, and whether Knudsen should replace one of the three names if the priority question goes against Mojsov.
Whether the omission of a second part is the right call, given that B024 is clean on attribution but early in clinical relevance, and B009 is unresolved on Eshhar and durability.
statement.conflict_note: I have no documented connection to any B012, B024 or B009 credited name. I have co-authored with Sten Linnarsson (eight joint works per OpenAlex, unaudited) and Jonas Frisen, none connected to a shortlisted candidate, and I share Karolinska Institutet with several colleagues on the committee. I use single-cell methods in my own research, which is a subject interest and not a personal tie to any candidate. I would disclose any connection that emerged and see no recusal-level conflict.
